_comment: The curated universe. A public app must never let a visitor trigger an
arbitrary fetch, so this file is the complete list of what exists.
`python -m btb.data build` ingests exactly this and nothing else.
HISTORY IS TIERED BY TIMEFRAME, on purpose. Fine timeframes get less
history than coarse ones, for a research reason before a cost one: 5m bars
from 2012 Bitstamp describe a market that no longer exists (2.7% of those
bars have zero range and zero volume). A 5m strategy validated on them is
validated against microstructure nobody trades today. The tiers are in
btb/data/ingest.py:HISTORY_YEARS and are recorded per series.
EQUITY INTRADAY IS SEVERELY CAPPED BY THE SOURCE. Yahoo serves 58 days of
5m/15m/30m and 725 days of 1h, measured. Those series are ingested so the
pipeline is exercised end to end, and they will carry a thin-sample
warning. They are NOT adequate for research. Fixing that needs Alpaca
(free key, minute data back to 2016) and is tracked as an open item.
Bitstamp has no 4h gap and no 2h-vs-4h ambiguity; Yahoo has no 4h at all,
which is why the crypto and equity timeframe lists differ.
